text.overview: A 4-pitch 5.7 crack climb up Himmelhorn's northwest aspect from the Himmelhorn-Ottohorn col, built around a striking 12-inch-wide vertical crack on pitch 2; widely regarded as one of the best moderate alpine rock climbs in the North Cascades.
text.descent: Early in the season, straightforward reverse scrambling suffices. Later in the season, rappel anchors found in the moats are helpful; a single 60m rope is workable with planning, though double ropes give more flexibility. An alternative is a series of rappels and exposed scrambling down the NW side back toward the col.

waypoints.name: Wild Hair Crack start (Himmelhorn-Ottohorn col area)
waypoints.directions: From the Goodell Creek trailhead, about 600 ft, take the Stump Hollow approach and cross into Crescent Creek Basin, with good bivy sites below Mount Terror. From the basin climb the narrow gully to the Himmelhorn-Ottohorn col, snow early in the season and icy snow and moats later, then scramble about 50 ft east of the col to where the rock turns near vertical.

waypoints.directions: Climb the twin cracks, the right-hand one preferred, then the signature vertical crack, sparsely protected for its first 20 ft. Easy scrambling leads to a notch just below the false summit, then an exposed ridge with airy low-5th moves reaches the summit block.

text.approach: From the Lightning Creek trailhead on Ross Lake, the first-ascent party hiked east past Willow Lake, then left the trail to bushwhack through timber and avalanche debris, crossed a ravine, and climbed steep dirt and brush to open timber on the broad shoulder south of the peak. They reached meadows near 5,000 ft and bypassed cliff bands to a saddle at about 6,200 ft below the buttress — roughly six hours from the trailhead — where they bivouacked.

This gains a rib/gully system leading to a high camp or bivy around 4,900-5,000 ft, and on to a saddle reported at roughly 6,800 ft below the final pitches.

text.approach: A two-stage approach and the second stage is the part that stops people. Day one is a long haul of 11-plus miles under heavy loads from the road to a camp just north of the peak - the same Hozomeen Ridge / border-swath ground used by the north-side scrambling routes, reached from Silver-Skagit Road out of Hope, B.C. From that camp the approach to the base took the first ascent party a tedious and painstaking 4.5 hours: downclimb a loose third-class gully, which the party described as dangerous but the lesser of the two evils, then cross several precipitous rocky ribs and steep, unstable ground to traverse into the launch point below the wall. Budget the base approach as a half-day objective in its own right and do it in daylight. Confirm the NPS border-gate status before planning; the crossing at Hozomeen has been closed to vehicles and foot traffic since 2020, with no end date given on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026.
